<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

**The assurer and the analyst shall be independent.** What varies is the degree of separation, which
depends on the importance of the output and the size and complexity of the analysis.

**Four bands, drawn around the work, each one containing the one inside it.**

**Level 1 Standard, the innermost band: a colleague, within your team.** Close enough to understand
the work without a handover, far enough to not have written it.

**Level 2 Enhanced: someone who had no hand in producing the work.** Still inside the team, but with
no stake in the answer being right the first time.

**Level 3 Comprehensive: an assurer from outside the delivering team.** Somebody whose judgement is
not shaped by the team's own habits and shortcuts.

**Level 4 BCA, the outermost band: a Lead Assurer from outside the delivering team, with external
review.** External review is what the band adds; the Lead Assurer sits where a Level 3 assurer does.

**Every level has somebody independent looking at the work.** The bands nest, so a reviewer who
satisfies one level also satisfies every level inside it. The question is how far out to go.

**Your own checks are the first line, not the last one.** Independence does not mean the analyst stops
assuring their own work. It means there shall also be formal independent assurance.

</details>
